action: I would correct an architecture paragraph and click Save edit while keeping its generated tables.
observed: Implementation review only; no interactions performed. sections.html warns that saving removes generated tables, and ChangeSection in sections.go unconditionally sets section.Tables = nil on save. There is no preserve-tables control.
problem: I cannot accomplish the combined goal of correcting prose and keeping generated tables through this editor, even when my correction does not concern the tables.
suggestion: Keep existing tables when saving prose and offer a separate explicit action to remove them.

action: I would edit two architecture sections, save the first, then follow a References link to check evidence.
observed: Implementation review only; no interactions performed. Every section has a separate native POST form without data-busy; forms.ts intercepts only form[data-busy]. The supplied implementation has no dirty-edit tracking, draft persistence, or navigation warning, while References and Document status are ordinary same-tab links.
problem: Only the submitted section's text is included in its form. My other unsaved changes have no protection when the page navigates, making a multi-section correction session easy to lose.
suggestion: Track unsaved sections and block navigation or another section's native submission until I save all changes or explicitly discard them.

action: I would use Regenerate to see whether a better architecture description is available after making manual corrections.
observed: Implementation review only; no interactions performed. Regenerate is adjacent to Save edit with the same button styling and no data-confirm. The regeneration branch in ChangeSection deletes the current section record and queues regeneration; the supplied UI offers no previous-version or undo control.
problem: A single click replaces my current saved section without a chance to retain it or compare it against the replacement, so trying regeneration risks losing useful edits.
suggestion: Keep the current section as a recoverable version and let me accept or reject the regenerated replacement.
